functions.name: FMovieScenePlaybackManager
functions.docs:
Describes whether to dissect looping when playing back a sequence.
Looping dissection means that, when a sequence loops, more than one evaluation context
is returned by the FMovieScenePlaybackManager::Update() methods: one context for updating
to the "last valid time", and one context for updating through the first few frames of
the next loop.

functions.name: FMovieScenePlaybackManager
functions.docs: Creates a playback manager immediately initialized with the given sequence.

functions.name: Initialize
functions.docs:
Initializes the playback manager for the given sequence.
This resets all playback settings (play rate, start/end offsets, etc.) to their default
values.

functions.name: Update
functions.signature: Update(Target, In Delta Seconds, Out Contexts)

functions.name: UpdateTo
functions.docs: As per the other Update method, but takes a time (in display rate) instead of seconds.

functions.name: UpdateAtCurrentTime
functions.docs:
Returns an evaluation context for the current time, i.e. using a zero-width evaluation
range set around the current time.

functions.name: GetCurrentTime
functions.docs: Gets the current playback position, in display rate.

functions.name: SetCurrentTime
functions.docs: Sets the current playback position, in display rate.

functions.name: GetEffectivePlaybackRange
functions.docs: Get the effective playback range, in display rate, taking into account start/end offsets.

functions.name: GetEffectiveStartTime
functions.docs: Get the effective playback start time, in display rate, taking into account any start offset.

functions.name: GetEffectiveEndTime
functions.docs: Get the effective playback end time, in display rate, taking into account any end offset.

functions.name: SetNumLoopsToPlay
functions.signature: SetNumLoopsToPlay(Target, In Num Loops To Play)
functions.docs: Sets the number of loops to play before ending playback.

functions.name: SetPingPongPlayback
functions.docs:
Sets whether the sequence should ping-pong between forwards and backwards playback.
Note that a "loop" is still one play through of the sequence, whether forwards or
backwards, so odd numbers of loops corresponds to a "ping" without a "pong".

functions.name: GetStartOffset
functions.docs: Gets the start offset of the playback in display rate.

functions.name: GetEndOffset
functions.docs: Gets the end offset of the playback in display rate.

functions.name: SetStartOffset
functions.docs: Sets the start offset of the playback in display rate.

functions.name: SetEndOffset
functions.docs: Sets the end offset of the playback in display rate.

functions.name: SetEndOffsetAsTime
functions.docs: Sets the end time of the playback in display rate.
